brief.headline: Push them to a maker's price — they're a reseller carrying a margin, and we have direct-source alternates lined up.

priceAsk.summary: Close the ₹3.37 L/yr gap to the best price we pay elsewhere, and benchmark their reseller price down toward a manufacturer's level.
priceAsk.target: ₹1.62/NOS on the LDPE bottle (our cheapest price today), saving ₹3.37 L/yr
priceAsk.basis: We pay Bprex ₹1.62/NOS for the same LDPE bottle; Berry charges ₹1.69/NOS — a 4.3% premium. They trade 100.0% of what they sell (no manufacturing), so their price carries a reseller margin. The market ask for a similar 28 mm cap sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc (MARKET-FAIR), with room to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume. We hold them to the maker's price we already pay, or bring in Manjushree or Mold-Tek direct.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 Days After Receipt — don't give them longer; they already stretch their own bills to 226d.

brief.financialLeverage: They're in bad shape: they lost ₹-22.50 Cr in FY2023-24, keep -199.2% of every rupee they sell (peers keep 2.3%), owe 220.44x their own cash, and score 1/10 on money-health. Their cash is stuck for 335d (peers 70d), so cash is very tight. But we're 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr in sales — losing us hurts. We can push on price because they're just a trader marking up a maker's goods, but push gently: a hard squeeze could tip a fragile supplier, so lead with the reseller-margin story and line up a backup before the meeting.

evidence.point: They keep far less profit than rivals
They're a pure reseller — no manufacturing
We're a big customer for them

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr); makes pharma bottles & caps direct — a strong second source, health 65/100.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-packaging leader (₹1010.97 Cr); profitable and healthy (73/100) — robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — pan-India manufacturer, medium confidence; potential direct maker for rigid plastics.

risks: They're fragile — losing money, deep in debt, distress-zone score. A hard price fight could break supply; don't squeeze until a backup is live.
They're a reseller, not a maker, so any supply hiccup traces back to their upstream source — another reason to qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek now.
We're 7.21% of their sales — big enough that they'll fight to keep us, but also big enough that losing us might tip them over if they're already on the edge.
Their cash is stuck for 335d vs 70d for peers, so they may delay orders or ask for advance payment if we push payment terms harder.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about bringing your price in line with the ₹1.62/NOS we pay Bprex, and making sure we're buying at a maker's level, not carrying a reseller margin.
